cause_quote: The original lookup returned a PR only through `if (open) { return open.url; }`, and the closed candidate was considered only if `candidate.body.includes(params.marker)`, so a closed PR carrying the first request’s marker fell through to the executor’s `if (!pullRequestUrl)` creation path.
user_saw: After GitHub accepted an update and the original PR closed, recovery could open a replacement PR or report a failure for the update that had already landed.
summary: The fix verifies and records accepted updates against the original PR before retrying publication, preserving later local work and allowing explicitly new requests after closure.
reasoning: The introducing diff already reused an open PR after pushing a new request’s commit, leaving the original request marker in the PR body. After an interruption and closure, that same diff ignored the accepted update’s closed PR and could create a replacement. I checked that the later repository backend carried forward the same lookup and creation fallback, while the guest-original-PR feature added a separate path for explicitly bound PRs.
